name: Holidays & Traditions
desc: Feasts, festivals and customs: Eid and Sham El Nessim, Diwali and Hanukkah, and how the world celebrates.

100: Which Egyptian spring holiday is celebrated with fesikh, coloured eggs and green onions?
Sham El Nessim
Which biscuits dusted with powdered sugar are baked in Egypt for Eid al-Fitr?
Kahk
What's the name of the lantern Egyptian children carry in Ramadan?
Fanous
What's the money given to children on Eid called in Egypt?
Eidiya
Which Eid is celebrated by sacrificing a sheep or cow?
Eid al-Adha
On which date do Egypt's Copts celebrate Christmas?
7 January
Which Hindu festival is famous for throwing coloured powder?
Holi
Which Hindu 'festival of lights' is celebrated with lamps and fireworks?
Diwali
Which Jewish holiday lasts eight nights and uses a nine-branched candlestick?
Hanukkah
Which American holiday in November is all about a turkey dinner?
Thanksgiving
Which Mexican holiday honours the dead with sugar skulls and marigolds?
Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos)
Which holiday on 31 October means costumes and trick-or-treating?
Halloween
Which festival is celebrated with dragon dances and red envelopes of money?
Chinese New Year (Lunar New Year)
On which date is Mother's Day celebrated in Egypt?
21 March
Which saint's day on 17 March turns everything green?
St Patrick's Day
Which day on 1 April is for pranks?
April Fools' Day
What do Americans celebrate on 4 July?
Independence Day
Which Brazilian city hosts the world's most famous carnival?
Rio de Janeiro
Which day on 14 February is for couples, chocolates and red roses?
Valentine's Day
What does the Ramadan 'mesaharati' do?
Walks the streets with a drum, waking people for suhoor
What's the meal eaten just before dawn in Ramadan called?
Suhoor
What's the sunset meal that breaks the fast in Ramadan called?
Iftar
Which Ramadan dessert is made of thin pastry threads baked with butter and soaked in syrup?
Konafa (kunafa)
Which small folded Ramadan pancakes are stuffed with nuts or cream?
Qatayef
What's the pilgrimage to Mecca in Dhul Hijjah, one of the five pillars of Islam, called?
Hajj
Which beer festival is held in Munich every autumn?
Oktoberfest
200: What's the name of the sweet sugar doll sold in Egypt for the Prophet's birthday?
Arouset el Moulid
Which fasting month ends with Eid al-Fitr?
Ramadan
What's the night in the last ten days of Ramadan said to be 'better than a thousand months'?
Laylat al-Qadr
What's fired every evening in Ramadan to tell Cairo it's time to break the fast?
The iftar cannon (Madfaa el Iftar)
What do Egyptians eat for Eid al-Adha lunch: rice, bread, garlicky vinegar sauce and meat?
Fatta
Which Thai festival is one huge water fight to celebrate the new year?
Songkran
Which Spanish town throws tonnes of tomatoes at each other every August in La Tomatina?
Buñol
What do Scots call New Year's Eve?
Hogmanay
Which British night on 5 November is all bonfires and fireworks?
Guy Fawkes Night (Bonfire Night)
Which day after Christmas is a holiday in the UK, named after the gift boxes given to servants?
Boxing Day
Which Persian New Year is celebrated on the first day of spring?
Nowruz
Which Jewish festival remembers the escape from Egypt, with a Seder meal?
Passover
Which day before Lent is famous for pancakes in Britain and parades in New Orleans?
Shrove Tuesday (Mardi Gras)
What's the French national day on 14 July called in English?
Bastille Day
Which Japanese spring tradition means picnicking under the cherry blossoms?
Hanami
What's the 15th day of Chinese New Year, with lanterns lit everywhere, called?
The Lantern Festival
Which month of the Islamic year is the month of Hajj?
Dhul Hijjah
Which Egyptian holiday on 6 October marks the 1973 crossing of the Suez Canal?
Armed Forces Day
What do the Dutch call Santa, who arrives by boat in November?
Sinterklaas
Which day, the eve of Eid al-Adha, is the most blessed day of the year to fast?
The Day of Arafah
Which Jewish coming-of-age ceremony is held for a boy at 13?
Bar mitzvah
What's the big Latin American celebration of a girl's 15th birthday called?
Quinceañera
Which Christian Sunday, a week before Easter, is called 'Had El Sa'af' in Egypt and is celebrated with woven palm fronds?
Palm Sunday
What's the charity Muslims must pay before the Eid al-Fitr prayer called?
Zakat al-Fitr
Which singer's 'Ya Leilet El Eid' is still played on every Eid?
Umm Kulthum
What's the Wednesday that starts Lent called?
Ash Wednesday
300: What's the horse-shaped sweet sold beside the Moulid sugar doll called?
Hosan el Moulid (the sugar horse)
Which ancient Egyptian festival gave Sham El Nessim its roots?
Shemu (the spring harvest festival)
What do Egyptians call the salted, fermented fish eaten on Sham El Nessim?
Fesikh
Which national holiday on 25 April marks Israel's last withdrawal from Sinai in 1982?
Sinai Liberation Day
Which Egyptian holiday on 23 July marks the 1952 revolution?
Revolution Day
Which day of Muharram is Ashura, when many Muslims fast?
The 10th
What's the night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and up to heaven called?
Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj
Which Jewish day of atonement is the holiest day of the year, a full day of fasting?
Yom Kippur
What's the Jewish New Year called?
Rosh Hashanah
Which African-American holiday from 26 December to 1 January has seven candles?
Kwanzaa
Which Alpine half-goat creature punishes naughty children around Christmas?
Krampus
Which Vietnamese holiday is their Lunar New Year?
Tết
Which Korean harvest festival is often called 'Korean Thanksgiving'?
Chuseok
Which Japanese summer festival welcomes back the spirits of ancestors?
Obon
Which Swedish festival in June has dancing around a maypole?
Midsummer (Midsommar)
In which month do Canadians celebrate Thanksgiving?
October
What do Spanish children celebrate on 6 January, when the Three Kings bring presents?
Three Kings' Day (Día de Reyes)
What's the 40-day period before Easter called?
Lent
Which Coptic fast before Christmas lasts 43 days, with no meat or dairy?
The Nativity Fast
Which Hindu festival celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters with a thread on the wrist?
Raksha Bandhan
Sham El Nessim always falls on the Monday after which holiday?
Coptic Easter
Which Scottish poet is celebrated on 25 January with haggis suppers?
Robert Burns (Burns Night)
Near Mecca, where do Hajj pilgrims stone the pillars that stand for the devil?
Mina
Which Spanish city's San Fermín festival is famous for the running of the bulls?
Pamplona
At an Egyptian 'Sebou' for a newborn, what is the baby gently shaken in?
A sieve (ghorbal)
Which Japanese holiday on 5 May is marked by flying carp-shaped streamers?
Children's Day (Kodomo no Hi)
400: Which Egyptian journalist started Egypt's Mother's Day in 1956?
Mustafa Amin
What is 'Wafaa El Nil', celebrated in August?
The festival of the Nile flood
Which date is Egypt's Police Day, the same day as the 2011 revolution?
25 January
What do Egyptians traditionally colour on Sham El Nessim morning?
Eggs
Which Islamic month comes right after Ramadan, when some fast six extra days?
Shawwal
Which Egyptian Ramadan street feast, often in a whole street, is laid on free for anyone breaking their fast?
Mawa'ed el Rahman
Which holiday marks the Prophet's birthday, on 12 Rabi' al-Awwal?
Al-Mawlid an-Nabawi
What's the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca that can be done at any time of year called?
Umrah
Which days of Dhul Hijjah are the 'Days of Tashreeq'?
The 11th, 12th and 13th
Which Indian festival honours the elephant-headed god with giant statues taken to the sea?
Ganesh Chaturthi
Which day is 'Pi Day', celebrated by maths fans?
What do people in Spain eat at midnight on New Year's Eve, one for each chime?
Twelve grapes
In which country is Saint Lucia's Day celebrated with girls wearing crowns of candles?
Sweden
Which Italian witch brings sweets to children on the night before 6 January?
La Befana
Which festival in Venice is famous for elaborate masks?
The Carnival of Venice
Which Mexican Christmas tradition re-enacts Mary and Joseph's search for shelter over nine nights?
Las Posadas
Which American holiday on the third Monday of January honours a civil-rights leader?
Martin Luther King Jr. Day
Which Jewish autumn festival is spent eating in a hut with a roof of branches?
Sukkot
What's the old Scottish name for going door to door in costume at Halloween?
Guising
What's the Islamic New Year's month called?
Muharram
What's 'I'tikaf'?
Staying in the mosque for worship, usually in Ramadan's last ten days
Which Coptic fast before Easter lasts 55 days?
The Great Lent
Which Jewish festival, seven weeks after Passover, marks the giving of the Torah?
Shavuot
Which singer's 'Ramadan Gana' is played on Egyptian TV every year when Ramadan starts?
Mohamed Abdel Muttalib
Which Christian feast, 40 days after Easter, marks Jesus rising up to heaven?
Ascension Day
In which American tradition on 2 February does a rodent 'predict' whether spring comes early?
Groundhog Day
500: In which Egyptian city does the Moulid of El-Sayed El-Badawi draw millions every year?
Tanta
Which Cairo mosque is at the heart of the Moulid of El-Hussein?
Al-Hussein Mosque
Which Luxor saint's moulid is held for the man whose mosque sits on top of Luxor Temple?
Abu el-Haggag
Which Fatimid-era story says Cairo's Ramadan lanterns began when people lit the way for which caliph?
Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah
What is 'Kiahk' in the Coptic calendar?
The month before Coptic Christmas, famous for its night praises
Which ancient Egyptian festival in Thebes carried Amun's statue from Karnak to Luxor Temple?
The Opet Festival
What is the Coptic New Year called, celebrated in September?
Nayrouz
Which Coptic feast in January, the baptism of Christ, is celebrated with taro and sugarcane?
Epiphany (Eid El Ghitas)
Which Indonesian island marks Nyepi, a 'day of silence' when even the airport shuts?
Bali
Which Japanese festival on 3 March celebrates girls with displays of dolls?
Hinamatsuri
What do the Chinese eat at the Mid-Autumn Festival?
Mooncakes
Which Scottish New Year tradition says the first person through your door should be a tall, dark man?
First-footing
Which country celebrates 'Koningsdag', when everyone dresses in orange?
The Netherlands
What is 'Up Helly Aa' in Shetland?
A fire festival where a Viking longship is burned
Which Hindu festival's name means 'nine nights', honouring the goddess Durga?
Navratri
In which country is Anzac Day, 25 April, a national day of remembrance (along with New Zealand)?
Australia
Which Jewish festival, celebrated with costumes and noisemakers, retells the story of Queen Esther?
Purim
Which Thai festival floats small decorated baskets on rivers under the full moon?
Loy Krathong
What do Ethiopians call their Christmas, celebrated on 7 January?
Genna (Ledet)
Which German city is famous for the oldest Christmas market, the Striezelmarkt?
Dresden
Which Russian week of feasting before Lent is all about pancakes (blini)?
Maslenitsa
In which Indian state is Onam, the harvest festival with flower carpets and snake-boat races, the biggest holiday?
Kerala
Which Sikh festival in April marks the founding of the Khalsa?
Vaisakhi
What does Iran's 'Yalda Night' celebrate?
The longest night of the year (winter solstice)
Which 15-day Coptic fast in August honours the Virgin Mary?
The Fast of the Virgin (Saint Mary's Fast)
Which Saudi holiday on 22 February marks the state's beginnings in 1727?
Founding Day (Yawm al-Ta'sis)
